findings.claim: The sidecar rewrite broke the hash check. The plan now leaves rewritten blog-scraper sidecars (and the 26 shared keys) out of the hash check, checks them on their own (each present at its blogs/ key, no blog-scraper/ text under blogs/), and gives the rewrite skip-existing semantics.

Images got no vector after vectors_only. spike:ov-carry-over/4 shows no re-index mode fixes it in 0.4.17.1 and that copying the old level-2 row (INSERT ... SELECT, no VLM call) makes find return the image and survives a later vectors_only. The plan copies the 52 old rows after the re-index and checks each one.

The plan promises that 'nomad job dispatch ov-carry-over re-runs it, and a re-run only adds missing keys', but only the blog-scraper copy uses --ignore-existing. clips, leo and blogs copy with plain rclone copy, which overwrites any target whose hash differs. After step 3 the merged blogs/ and blogs/<source>/ sidecars are regenerated on purpose, and once the instance is live, ov-clip and the blog scraper add files that make OpenViking rewrite parent .overview.md/.abstract.md under clips/ and blogs/. A re-run then puts the old sidecars back over the new ones without a word, and the 'rclone check --one-way' hash check fails on exactly those keys, so the re-run cannot exit 0 either. Fix: make every copy skip existing keys, and define what the hash check means once the target's sidecars have moved on. For example, on every run check only that non-sidecar files are present with the same hash, and that sidecars are present.
